ant.gateway: ant-gateway's router (testkit::build_router), built as antd builds it: no CORS origins and light mode, as Freedom configures Ant
ant.node_loop: a port of the node-loop arms these requests reach (ant-p2p src/behaviour.rs, same commit): GetChunkRaw, GetFeed, GetBytes, GetBytesEncrypted, run_stream_bytes and run_stream_bzz, over a memory chunk source, one attempt each (src/node.rs)
ant.missing_chunks: a miss the network corroborated: FetchExhausted, not starved, with 8 not-found answers
ant.writers: files: split_bytes_with_redundancy; manifests: build_single_file_manifest, build_collection_manifest, build_entries_manifest, build_feed_manifest; encrypted files: split_bytes_encrypted_with_keys; and, for shapes these can't make, the generator's own mantaray writer (src/mantaray.rs), held to Ant's on a manifest both write

node_headers.note: headers that describe the node, not the content: Ant's router adds `server: ant-gateway/0.5.71` to every answer

bee_cross_check.how: bee-check/: Bee's pipeline splits each file's content at its redundancy level, and Bee's upload handlers' manifest code writes the single-file, directory and feed manifests (bzz.go fileUploadHandler, dirs.go storeDir, feed.go feedPostHandler); run by hand, not in CI
bee_cross_check.why_they_differ: Ant's level-0 splitter wraps a level's lone leftover reference in an intermediate chunk of one reference, where Bee's hashtrie Sum carries it up unwrapped; the files marked lone_leaf_wrappers are Ant's trees, and their -bee cases are Bee's

formats.content: content(seed, n): SHA-256(seed ‖ u64_be(i)) for i = 0, 1, 2, …, concatenated and cut to n bytes. A file case's body is content(seed, size).
formats.key_stream: key_stream(label): the chunk keys of an encrypted split, in Ant's chunk-write order; key i is keccak256(label ‖ u32_be(i)). Ant pads the ciphertext with zeros when keys are injected.
formats.owner_secret: a feed owner's secp256k1 secret is keccak256(label), the label given with the feed.
formats.chunks: address (hex) → wire bytes (base64), for every chunk a reader needs that isn't a slice of some content: roots, intermediates, the wrappers Ant's splitter writes, manifest nodes, feed updates, encrypted chunks and the crafted shapes. A data leaf is rebuilt from its content: leaf i of a file of n bytes is u64_le(len) ‖ content[i·4096 .. min(n, (i+1)·4096)]. Parity chunks are left out: nothing reads them when nothing is missing.
formats.files: data trees from Ant's splitter, one per size and redundancy level: id, seed, size, redundancy, root, tree (the addresses Ant's joiner reads for the whole body, less the content's leaves: the root, then the rest by address), data_leaves, parities (chunks the split wrote that the join doesn't read), joined_equals_content (whether Ant's joiner reads the tree back as the content), and lone_leaf_wrappers where Ant's tree has them. A -bee case is the same content split as Bee splits it, where that differs.
formats.manifests: id, root, writer, nodes (the chunks of the manifest's nodes), entries, and lookups: ant-retrieval's lookup_path answer for each path, the resolved data_ref, content_type, metadata and feed, or the error's text.
formats.feeds: sequence feeds: owner, topic, manifest (build_feed_manifest), manifest_nodes, and updates (index, address, id, version, and the reference or root the update names). v1 updates wrap u64_be(timestamp) ‖ reference, timestamps counted from meta.clock_unix; v2 updates wrap the root chunk itself.
formats.shapes: trees Ant reads that a simple reader wouldn't, each a root over two leaves whose second leaf's span or payload differs from the 60 bytes its parent gives it.
formats.exchanges: requests through Ant's gateway and its answers: id (case#n), case, note, request (method, path, headers; every bzz request carries meta.request_headers), response (status, headers in Ant's order, and body). A body is {length: 0}, {content: {seed, from, length}} for a slice of content(seed, …), {base64} up to 64 KiB, or {length, sha256}. A multipart boundary, which Ant draws at random, is written {boundary} in the header and the body.
